page: The Vultr vhf-2c-2gb is an entry-tier virtual machine belonging to the High Frequency Compute family. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it is powered by an Intel processor operating at 2.0 GHz. The instance allocates two shared vCPUs derived from a single physical core via hyper-threading. The CPU cache subsystem includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 4 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of L3 cache. It incorporates instruction set extensions such as AVX, AES, BMI2, and FMA, while omitting AVX-512 and AMX extensions. Complementing the compute resources are 2.0 GB of system memory, providing an allocation of 1.0 GB per vCPU.

Storage consists of 80 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD capacity. No discrete GPU accelerators are included. Network connectivity features one complimentary public IPv4 address. Across synthetic CPU benchmarks, the server registers average single-core throughput, achieving a score of 1425.29 in stress-ng and 24.24 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip compression. However, due to its shared single-core hyper-threaded topology, multi-threaded CPU output remains constrained, with a multi-core stress-ng score of 2786.09 and an aggregate PassMark CPU score of 3137.23.

Memory throughput exhibits noticeable boundaries under larger datasets, dropping from 195.55 GB/sec for small cached 16 KB read blocks to 18.67 GB/sec read and 12.65 GB/sec write for uncached 256 MB blocks. Benchmark results reflect these hardware characteristics, reporting 2.3 million Redis SET operations per second and 2.3 GB/sec throughput for static web delivery. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the instance provides high local NVMe storage density and capable baseline single-thread execution relative to its resource tier.

Given the shared virtual core topology, 2.0 GB memory limit, and moderate throughput under concurrent load, the vhf-2c-2gb is best suited for lightweight web serving, low-traffic API endpoints, small background workers, utility microservices, and development environments.
description: The Vultr vhf-2c-2gb is a budget compute instance from the High Frequency Compute tier, powered by an Intel x86_64 processor operating at 2.0 GHz. It provides 2 shared vCPUs mapped to 1 physical hyper-threaded core, supported by 2.0 GB of RAM and 80 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage. The CPU features 16 MB of L3 cache, along with AVX, AES, and BMI2 instruction support, though it lacks AVX-512. Benchmark results show average single-threaded execution, registering 1425.29 on stress-ng and 24.24 GB/sec in gzip compression, while multi-threaded capacity and memory bandwidth remain modest due to shared execution units. Delivering cost-effective local storage density and balanced entry-level processing, the vhf-2c-2gb is appropriate for lightweight web serving, low-throughput microservices, development sandboxes, and auxiliary infrastructure tasks.
